metadata.title: Monoclonal Antibodies: Streamlined Nonclinical Safety Studies: Draft Guidance for Industry
metadata.topic: Draft guideline · FDA human drugs and biologics
metadata.legal_basis: FDA Guidance Document (21 CFR 10.115). Guidance states FDA's current thinking and is not binding unless a statute or regulation requires it; the official text governs.

candidates.statement: In general, FDA’s guidance documents do not establish legally enforceable responsibilities. 50 Instead, guidances describe the Agency’s current thinking on a topic and should be viewed only 51 as recommendations, unless specific regulatory or statutory requirements are cited. The use of 52 the word should in Agency guidances means that something is suggested or recommended but 53 not required. 54
candidates.context: This guidance does not address toxicology studies related to multispecific antibodies, conjugated 46 antibodies (e.g., antibody-drug conjugates), or antibody constructs (e.g., single-chain variable 47 fragments) 48

candidates.statement: For exceptional cases when a 3-month study and WoE risk assessment may be inadequate , 121 sponsors should consult the appropriate FDA review division regarding whether a 6-month 122 toxicology study is warranted. For duration of general toxicology studies in severely 123 debilitating or life-threatening hematologic disorders see the guidance for industry Severely 124 Debilitating or Life-Threatening Hematologic Disorders: Nonclinical Development of 125 Pharmaceuticals . 126
candidates.context: • Other nonclinical data as scientifically justified (e.g., NAMs, transgenic models, data 118 using surrogates). 119 2. Examples of When 3-Month (or Longer Duration) Toxicology Studies Are Not 128 Warranted 129 When an assessment of long-term safety is warranted (e.g., a monospecific antibody being 130 administered weekly continuously to humans over many months), sponsors should decide 131 whether a 3-month (or longer duration) toxicology study in animals will generate relevant 132 information. Below are examples of when 3-month studies (or studies of longer duration) are 133 not warranted. The concept may be applied to other safety studies, as appropriate, and 134 sponsors should discuss their nonclinical development plans with the FDA review divisions 135 before initiating a study in NHPs. 136

candidates.statement: • Animal toxicology studies should use pharmacologically relevant species. Pharmacology 157 studies should demonstrate binding of the monospecific antibody to the molecular target 158 and elicit the intended functional effects. In the absence of a pharmacologically relevant 159 species, the safety assessment could be based on a WoE risk assessment in lieu of animal 160 toxicology studies . 161
